sent_to_model:
Last month I told Dana on the Circle forum that I would write up Harbor Point once my writer had been through a real trial. It has now survived eight days of a civil trial, so I owe her, and everyone else, that review. Please draft it as a new post on the Vendor Reviews board. The moderator's pinned post spells out what she wants included, and the work order, the battery emails and the invoice are all in my inbox. Do not post it; leave it as a draft and I will read it over tonight with a cup of tea. It should be fair to Gloria, who did good work, without pretending the phone situation is anything other than what it is.

- picked up Tues 10/27, so 6 business days against the 10 quoted
- paid for it myself, as I do all my equipment; no reimbursement from the court
- Harbor Point is a two-person shop off York Road, parking in back is free
- first full day back was expert testimony, an engineer who talks in numbers; number bar did not double a single stroke
- called Wed 10/21 to ask about progress, rang out, no voicemail box set up; Gloria emailed the following day
- loaner's tilt arm slipped mid-afternoon during a deposition, propped it on a legal pad for the rest of the day
- machine came back with a printed one-page service sheet listing every adjustment, which I have never had from anyone
- $310 is fair for what was done, and she asked before adding the battery, which matters to me
- phone hours (Tues–Thurs, 9–4 only) are the real weakness for anyone working a Monday docket
- Dana should come away knowing whether to trust them with her Aria
- measured, the way I would want to read it myself; no gushing, no grudges

(About me: court stenographer who writes crime novels, 52, Baltimore, Maryland. Length: all the messages together should come to roughly 400-800 words.)
